verdict.summary: Any GitLab user can register an OAuth application (user, group or instance level) and any GitLab.com user can authorize it the same day: there's no review, verification or marketplace. The work is in token handling (2-hour access tokens with rotating refresh tokens) and in self-managed instances, where each customer's GitLab needs its own application registration.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Add an application with a redirect URI and scopes, then run authorization code + PKCE. No verification step is documented.

timeToProd.assumes: A GitLab.com OAuth app requesting read_api or api to read and act on users' projects; self-managed customers add per-instance registration time.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The provider docs describe no approval or review requirement for applications.

prerequisites.item: A GitLab.com account (or Owner role on a group for a group-owned app)
prerequisites.why: Applications are owned by a user, a group (Owner role needed) or, on self-managed, the instance (admin needed).

prerequisites.item: A redirect URI that exactly matches what your client sends
prerequisites.why: GitLab compares the redirect URI exactly.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Stated in the MCP pre-registered app section.

prerequisites.item: For self-managed or Dedicated customers: an application registered on their instance
prerequisites.why: OAuth applications live on a specific GitLab instance, so a gitlab.com client ID doesn't work elsewhere.

scopeTiers.impact: Sign-in and basic profile. Not enough for reading projects.

scopeTiers.tier: Read access to projects and code
scopeTiers.impact: Read groups, projects, issues and merge requests via the API, and private repositories over Git HTTP or the Repository Files API. Good default for a read-only agent.
Create issues, comment, open merge requests, push code. Broad: api covers groups, projects, registries and packages.

scopeTiers.time: Same day (if the group allows MCP)
scopeTiers.impact: mcp is required for the GitLab MCP server at /api/v4/mcp; legacy PATs are rejected. An admin or top-level group owner must allow MCP access first.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: ai_workflows seen only in live scopes_supported; not described in the docs we read.

scopeTiers.impact: Only meaningful when the authorizing user is an administrator, typically on self-managed instances.

steps.title: Sign in and open Applications
steps.detail: Go to Edit profile > Access > Applications > Add new application (or a group's Settings > Applications for a group-owned app).

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: URL returned 302 to /users/sign_in on 2026-10-20; we didn't sign in.

steps.title: Choose the scopes
steps.detail: Pick least privilege: read_api (+ read_repository) for read-only agents, api for write actions, mcp if using the MCP server, openid for sign-in.

steps.title: Create the application
steps.detail: Enter name, redirect URI and scopes; leave Confidential checked for server-side apps (clear it for public/PKCE-only clients). Copy the Application ID and Secret.

steps.title: Implement authorization code + PKCE
steps.detail: Redirect to https://gitlab.com/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, state, scope and an S256 code_challenge. Exchange at POST https://gitlab.com/oauth/token with the code_verifier.

steps.title: Handle refresh-token rotation
steps.detail: Access tokens expire after 2 hours by default. A refresh invalidates both old tokens and returns new ones, so store the new refresh token atomically.

steps.title: Support self-managed instances
steps.detail: Let users enter their GitLab base URL, and store per-instance client credentials (or use DCR where the instance allows it).

steps.title: Ask customers to register your app on their instance
steps.detail: For self-managed customers, an admin creates an instance-wide application (optionally trusted, which skips the consent screen) and shares the credentials with you.

steps.title: Optionally use the MCP server
steps.detail: Connect to https://gitlab.com/api/v4/mcp with an mcp-scoped token. MCP clients can self-register via DCR at https://gitlab.com/oauth/register (10 registrations per IP per hour).

steps.title: Plan for rate limits
steps.detail: Handle 429s with backoff. GitLab has published proposed per-user and per-group limits (e.g. Free 5,000/hour per user); MCP is limited to 60/min (Free) or 600/min (Premium/Ultimate) per user.

agentCanDo: Implement authorization code + PKCE and rotating refresh
Build per-instance base URL and credential handling
Register MCP clients via DCR and handle 429 backoff
humanMustDo: Sign in and create the application, copying the secret
Customer side: top-level group owner enables MCP access if using MCP
Customer side: self-managed admins register an instance-wide app

blockers.symptom: 'The redirect URI included is not valid.' on the authorize page
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri doesn't exactly match the application's registered URI.
blockers.fix: Register the exact URI and send it identically in authorize and token requests.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: Exact-match rule is sourced; the error wording is from memory of GitLab's Doorkeeper UI and wasn't checked.

blockers.cause: Refresh tokens rotate; reusing an old one fails.
blockers.fix: Persist the newest refresh token after each refresh and serialise refreshes.

blockers.cause: Using a legacy personal/project/group access token or an OAuth token without the mcp scope.
blockers.fix: Request the mcp scope in OAuth, or use a fine-grained PAT with the MCP tool permission.

blockers.symptom: MCP clients fail to register behind a corporate VPN
blockers.cause: DCR is limited to 10 registrations per IP per hour, or an admin disabled DCR.
blockers.fix: Use a pre-registered OAuth application (mcp scope, Confidential cleared).

blockers.symptom: MCP tools unavailable for some users
blockers.cause: The top-level group (GitLab.com) or instance hasn't allowed MCP server access.
blockers.fix: Ask a group owner or admin to enable it.

blockers.cause: Per-user, per-group or per-IP limits on GitLab.com.
blockers.fix: Back off using the rate-limit headers and spread work over time.

nuances.text: Access tokens expire after 2 hours by default; self-managed and Dedicated admins can change the lifetime (GitLab 19.1+).
Device authorization grant is GA (17.9+), and gitlab.com also advertises client_credentials and PKCE (plain and S256) in its discovery document.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: grant_types and code_challenge_methods observed in openid-configuration on 2026-10-20.

nuances.text: GitLab has published new per-user and per-top-level-group rate limits that are proposed but not yet in effect, with brownouts announced in advance. Plan for Free users at 5,000 requests/hour.
Groups with SAML SSO may require passing root_namespace_id on the authorize request.
Instance-wide applications can be marked trusted, which skips the consent screen for that instance's users.
Applications created through the REST API don't enforce PKCE, and GitLab doesn't verify which client uses a given client ID.
